#!/bin/bash
#FLUX: --job-name=mesh_nbody_benchmark
#FLUX: -N 1
#FLUX: -n 4
#FLUX: --tasks-per-node=4
#FLUX: --cpus-per-task=10
#FLUX: --gpus-per-task=1
#FLUX: -t 00:15:00
#FLUX: --output=mesh_nbody_benchmark_%j.out
#FLUX: --error=mesh_nbody_benchmark_%j.out
#FLUX: --mail-user=denise.lanzieri@cea.fr

# Omitted Slurm option: --hint=nomultithread.
# Flux does not have a direct equivalent to disable hyperthreading at the job level.
# This may affect performance if the system has hyperthreading enabled by default.
# CPU affinity may need to be managed manually if this is critical.

# Omitted Slurm option: -A ftb@gpu.
# Account/project specification is not a standard Flux job directive.
# This is typically handled by site-specific queue policies or configurations.

# Omitted Slurm option: --qos=qos_gpu-dev.
# Quality of Service is managed by submitting to a specific queue in Flux,
# e.g., 'flux submit -Q qos_gpu-dev ...'

# nettoyage des modules charges en interactif et herites par defaut
module purge

# chargement des modules
module load tensorflow-gpu/py3/2.4.1+cuda-11.2 nvidia-nsight-systems/2021.1.1
#module load tensorflow-gpu/py3/2.4.1+nccl-2.8.3-1

# echo des commandes lancees
set -x

# JZ FIX
# The JOBSCRATCH environment variable is specific to Slurm.
# You may need to replace this with a path appropriate for your Flux environment.
export TMPDIR=$JOBSCRATCH
ln -s $JOBSCRATCH /tmp/nvidia
# execution du code avec binding via bind_gpu.sh : 1 GPU pour 1 tache MPI.

#srun nvprof --profile-child-processes -f -o result-mesh_nbody-%p.nvvp /gpfslocalsup/pub/idrtools/bind_gpu.sh python -u mesh_nbody_benchmark.py --nc=512 --batch_size=1 --nx=2 --ny=2 --hsize=32

# execution du code avec binding via bind_gpu.sh : 1 GPU pour 1 tache MPI.
# Note: The 'srun' command has been replaced with 'flux run'.
# The per-task output format string '%t' has been replaced with Flux's '{{task.id}}'.
# The SLURM_TASK_PID variable has been replaced with Flux's '{{task.id}}' for unique naming.
flux run --mpi=pmi2 -o mesh_nbody_{{task.id}}.log /gpfslocalsup/pub/idrtools/bind_gpu.sh nsys profile --stats=true -t nvtx,cuda,mpi -o result-{{task.id}} python -u mesh_nbody_benchmark.py  --nc=128 --batch_size=1 --nx=2 --ny=2 --hsize=32 --nsteps=3

reasons: The format specifier '%j' used in '--output' and '--error' directives is invalid for Flux. The correct format is '{{id}}' or '{{jobid}}'.
The '--mail-user' directive is not a standard Flux job option. Mail notifications are typically handled through site-specific configurations or wrappers.
issues: The script uses the environment variable '$JOBSCRATCH', which is specific to Slurm and will likely be undefined in a Flux environment, causing 'export TMPDIR' and 'ln -s' commands to fail or behave incorrectly.

The resource geometry (-N 1, -n 4, --tasks-per-node=4) is consistent. However, the total resource request is 40 CPUs (4 tasks * 10 cpus) and 4 GPUs (4 tasks * 1 gpu) on a single node, which should be verified against the available hardware configurations.

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=mesh_nbody_benchmark   # nom du job
##SBATCH --partition=gpu_p2          # de-commente pour la partition gpu_p2
#SBATCH --ntasks=4                  # nombre total de tache MPI (= nombre total de GPU)
#SBATCH --nodes=1                  # number of nodes
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=4          # nombre de tache MPI par noeud (= nombre de GPU par noeud)
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:4                 # nombre de GPU par nœud (max 8 avec gpu_p2)
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=10           # nombre de coeurs CPU par tache (un quart du noeud ici)
##SBATCH --cpus-per-task=3           # nombre de coeurs CPU par tache (pour gpu_p2 : 1/8 du noeud)
# /!\ Attention, "multithread" fait reference a l'hyperthreading dans la terminologie Slurm
#SBATCH --hint=nomultithread         # hyperthreading desactive
#SBATCH --time=00:15:00              # temps d'execution maximum demande (HH:MM:SS)
#SBATCH --output=mesh_nbody_benchmark_%j.out # nom du fichier de sortie
#SBATCH --error=mesh_nbody_benchmark_%j.out  # nom du fichier d'erreur (ici commun avec la sortie)
#SBATCH -A ftb@gpu                   # specify the project
#SBATCH --mail-user=denise.lanzieri@cea.fr    # send mail to user
#SBATCH --qos=qos_gpu-dev            # using the dev queue, as this is only for profiling

# nettoyage des modules charges en interactif et herites par defaut
module purge

# chargement des modules
module load tensorflow-gpu/py3/2.4.1+cuda-11.2 nvidia-nsight-systems/2021.1.1
#module load tensorflow-gpu/py3/2.4.1+nccl-2.8.3-1

# echo des commandes lancees
set -x

# JZ FIX
export TMPDIR=$JOBSCRATCH
ln -s $JOBSCRATCH /tmp/nvidia
# execution du code avec binding via bind_gpu.sh : 1 GPU pour 1 tache MPI.

#srun nvprof --profile-child-processes -f -o result-mesh_nbody-%p.nvvp /gpfslocalsup/pub/idrtools/bind_gpu.sh python -u mesh_nbody_benchmark.py --nc=512 --batch_size=1 --nx=2 --ny=2 --hsize=32

# execution du code avec binding via bind_gpu.sh : 1 GPU pour 1 tache MPI.
srun --unbuffered --mpi=pmi2 -o mesh_nbody_%t.log /gpfslocalsup/pub/idrtools/bind_gpu.sh nsys profile --stats=true -t nvtx,cuda,mpi -o result-%q{SLURM_TASK_PID} python -u mesh_nbody_benchmark.py  --nc=128 --batch_size=1 --nx=2 --ny=2 --hsize=32 --nsteps=3
